Welcome to /v/Djent's album discussion! This week we are looking at Northlane's brand new full-length album "Node". If you haven't heard it yet, you can stream the album here.

Feel free to share your opinions, compare it to other albums, etc. All discussion related to the album or Northlane is welcome. Be sure to also suggest what album you want to be discussed next week! A couple days late to the discussion? No problem! Feel free to share your thoughts anyways, this is a continuous week-long discussion. Try to include a rating out of 10 and your favorite track!

This week should be fun. Everyone loves discussing new vocalists. This discussion will go into next Friday, and next week's discussion will go into the next Wednesday. I think next week we should do an After the Burial album in memoriam of Justin Lowe's recent death.

Well I just finished listening to it. I feel like this may be the minority opinion, but I really enjoyed it. The only other Northlane album I've listened to was Discoveries, which I honestly thought was pretty meh. It didn't really capture me and the songs sounded the same to me, but maybe I just haven't listened to it enough. However, with Node, I was immediately intrigued by all the songs, and thought it was a very good contrast to Discoveries. It seems like they have really evolved their sound, and instead of being Architect-worship, they made their own thing, and I really enjoy it. I think the clean vocals suit the songs very well, and the screams actually very faintly reminded me of black metal vocals in some parts (which is awesome, because I love black metal). Surprisingly, they seem to have added a lot more elements that reminded me of TesseracT, and the guitar tones reminded me of Cloudkicker. In one sense, I think they sounded like a more ambient version of Periphery. The songs didn't sound all that much different than each other, but I thought it worked for the overall feel of the album. Node also didn't really blow me away with any insane riffage, or vocalization, but it all mixed together in a very interesting way and the melodies felt very fresh to me. I found the drumming to be very interesting. It was very creative, heavily-jazz influenced drumming, that really caught my attention, and I'm a bassist. The bass and drum parts I loved. Node seemed to have taken a lot of cool stuff from various other groups and combined it with their own sound. It was a unique experience, and definitely my favorite release from them so far. And, sorry, but I like Marcus much better than the old vocalist, especially with the cleans. I remember listening to Discoveries and thinking that the vocals didn't vary much from song to song, and the album could've really used some clean passages, which it had none of. Node was actually both what I expected Northlane to be, but also great stuff I wouldn't have ever expected from them. Overall, Node did exactly what an album should do, and I was left very satisfied. The album felt very "complete" to me. Still, satisfied does not mean blown away, and I think there is definitely more potential for the band.

I rate Node a 7.25/10 and my favorite track is Rot.

Looking for a good flight simulator, can anyone recommend one?

I've been flight simming since the days of subLOGIC FS II on a Commodore 64. I've used every version of MSFS, X-plane since v8, Fly! when that was out, Falcon 4.0, Tornado and others. For general aviation simulation, there are really only three options:

  • MSFS X
  • Lockheed Martin's Prepar3D (P3D)
  • X-Plane 10 (XP10)

MSFS X is long in the tooth and unsupported. On the other hand, it has a phenomenal third-party add-on ecosystem. The flight modeling doesn't strike me as particularly realistic (I'm not a private pilot, but have spent time flying), giving a "plane on rails" sensation for me.

P3D is LM's licensed extension of MSFS X. I have not tried it, but from what I've read, some claim the flight modeling is more realistic. That may just be anecdotal, however. A lot of the third-party MSFS X add-ons and aircraft will work with it, as it's essentially a rebooted MSFS X. Their licensing model may or may not work for you. I understand it's also not cheap.

XP10 is under continual, active development. The fans of XP are vociferous, bordering on rabid (see: x-plane.org, which is not affiliated with Laminar Research) and quirky. Third-party add-ons and aircraft have steadily increased in quality and availability over the last five years. The flight model, to me, seems much more realistic. The lighting is not, but you can't have it all. Weather system out of the box is pretty basic.

MSFS and P3D are Windows-only. XP10 will run on Windows, OSX and Linux (Linux support is spotty, though, especially in regard to third-party kit). I have MSFS X still, but I haven't actually flown it in many years. XP10, in combination with an account on the PilotEdge network for real-time/close to real-life ATC is a great combination for me. XP10 isn't terribly expensive and can be had from a variety of sources (including Steam). If you do decide to buy via Steam, there may be some additional work getting third-party aircraft/add-ons installed relative to a plain-vanilla XP10 install. The forums at x-plane.org and x-pilot.com can help with that, though.

I absolutely love dwarf gourami, their natural colors are just stunning. Sadly I've had pretty bad experiences with them. I've tried twice with at least a year in between. Both times they seemed to do very well for a couple of weeks, then you would start to notice this little bump somewhere, this would develop in a small ulcer quite quickly and death would follow not long after that.

Apparently most captive bred dwarf gourami now carry some kind of lethal iridovirus that seems impossible to kill unless you also kill the fish. I'd stay off of them for a while until that situation is solved, unless you have a local breeder or something.

I've had quite some succes keeping a betta with medium shrimp like ghost shrimp and amanos. Some of the wildtype betta's are actually pretty cool, I mean, I wish I could have a betta mahachaiensis but I can't get another tank and it doesn't really fit with the existing ones.

But I was never able to keep rcs with betta or gourami or even most small tetra. I think a combination of kuhli loaches and hatchet fish might be and look cool with rcs, though I'm not sure about hatchet's needs so I'm not sure if it's actually doable. Check aqadvisor.com to test basic comptability and tank size requirements. (Yes this site throws you back to the mid nineties, but it has some good info. It's not the bible and you always need additional research but it's a good starting point to get a general idea if your project is doable or not.)
